question: The rate of change of momentum of an object is proportional to the applied unbalanced force in the direction of the force. This rule is known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Newton's Second Law of Motion**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion** states that the **rate of change of momentum of an object is proportional to the applied unbalanced force **in the direction of the force.
 
• This law can be mathematically represented as **F = m.a**, were F is the force applied, m is the mass of the object, and a is the acceleration.
 
• It implies that an **object will accelerate in the direction of the applied force**, and the magnitude of the acceleration is directly proportional to the force and inversely proportional to the mass of the object.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion** states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• **Newton's Third Law of Motion** states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
• These laws of motion were formulated by Sir Isaac Newton and are fundamental to classical mechanics.
